The following resources accompany the Methods for Dummies series at the 2026 Southern Management Association annual meeting. Resources are grouped by presenter/topic. Click any DOI link to go straight to the article, or the publisher page for books/chapters.

Resources marked <span class="badge-start">Start here</span> are a suggested "first read" within each topic.

## CFA, EFA, and Model Fit (Dr. Andrew Hanna)

::: {.section-intro}
Articles and chapters covering everything from exploratory analysis through model fit.
:::

::: {.resource .start-here}
<span class="badge-start">Start here</span>

Williams, L. J., & Hanna, A. A. (2023). Exploratory/confirmatory factor analysis and scale development. In L. R. Ford & T. A. Scandura (Eds.), *The SAGE handbook of survey development and application*. SAGE.

[Download a free copy of the chapter here](Williams-Hanna-2023-Factor-Analysis.pdf){.link}

Covers how exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis fit together in developing and evaluating survey scales. Includes a step-by-step guide to performing both types of factor analyses, with code for use in R.
:::

::: {.resource}
Brown, T. A. (2015). *Confirmatory factor analysis for applied research* (2nd ed.). Guilford Press.

[Publisher page (book, no DOI)](https://www.guilford.com/books/Confirmatory-Factor-Analysis-for-Applied-Research/Timothy-Brown/9781462515363){.link}

An applied, step-by-step book on specifying, estimating, evaluating, and revising CFA models, with worked examples.
:::

::: {.resource}
Costello, A. B., & Osborne, J. (2005). Best practices in exploratory factor analysis: Four recommendations for getting the most from your analysis. *Practical Assessment, Research, and Evaluation, 10*.

[https://doi.org/10.7275/jyj1-4868](https://doi.org/10.7275/jyj1-4868){.link}

A short, accessible demonstration of how choices about extraction, rotation, and retention change EFA results, with practical recommendations.
:::

::: {.resource .start-here}
<span class="badge-start">Start here</span>

Hu, L., & Bentler, P. M. (1999). Cutoff criteria for fit indexes in covariance structure analysis: Conventional criteria versus new alternatives. *Structural Equation Modeling, 6*(1), 1–55.

[https://doi.org/10.1080/10705519909540118](https://doi.org/10.1080/10705519909540118){.link}

The source of the most widely cited fit guidelines (for example CFI near .95, RMSEA near .06, SRMR near .08). Read it together with the next section.
:::
